cells.tense: The many truths are gathered here, and the telling of them is being done now.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: At the next shared decision, put your read on the table first — the piece you'd hold, the piece you'd let go, and the reason — before the back-and-forth starts. Say it once.
cells.core:
Most have to work to see what matters. Here it arrives already sorted, and the hard part isn't finding it but handing it over in a shape others can hold. Done right, you name a thing and it holds, and the argument about where to start stops.

What's been kept close is called caution, when it is only unfinished. Put your read on the table before anyone asks, at the next decision: the piece you'd keep, the piece you'd release, and the reason, once, nothing attached. What comes back can be answered. Seeing what matters is not the same as saying it, and the table is still waiting on the second half.
cells.sheetLine: Say the one truth you're steering by, plainly, once.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once, and needing to say which one leads
cells.place: where what is known gets sifted before it is spoken: the facing place, before there is a way to say it

lint.detail: the "say it once" close — the house medicine; vary how it is handed over

cells.tense: Every coming day is being arranged into a system that has not been asked to be lived in.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: When you catch yourself laying out the coming weeks, stop and turn toward the next choice only. Take it from one thing that guides you, and leave the rest unsurveyed for now.
cells.core:
At a distance, four or five futures can be seen at once, each workable, none chosen. From there, the days that have not arrived get organized — who ends up with what, how the difficult conversation will run, what gets said before anyone asks. It feels like foresight. It sits just in front of the thing it's foreseeing.

The correction is not a better plan. Catch yourself laying out the coming weeks, stop, and turn toward the next choice alone — take it from one thing that guides you, and leave the rest unsurveyed for now. Nothing at the seed stage needs straightening. But the coming week needs a heading, and none has been picked.
cells.sheetLine: You're arranging every unlit day instead of the one you're in.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once, and needing to say which one leads

cells.tense: The ability to see what mattered was present once, and standing at that door has become the stance.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Ask someone who was also there to work the same box, drawer, or list alongside you — out loud, together, once. Go through it with them instead of ahead of them.
cells.core:
That place still holds everything it held, and picking a piece up to decide doesn't happen. Standing at the door is what has replaced moving, since each thing touched seems to pick a side in something unfinished. The ability to see what matters is real. It has no outlet by itself.

What is thin isn't judgment. It's the one connection that can't be done alone. Join someone who was also there over the same box, drawer, or list — work it out loud, together, once, rather than ahead of them. Holding many truths with no one else present turns into standing still, and the shelf stays full.
cells.sheetLine: What you can see hasn't moved since that place closed.

cells.tense: The fair thing has been getting done by your hands while your own account of it stays silent.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: Pick one small open question that's been sitting — what's owed, what's fair here — and settle it from the quiet sense inside you. Act on it, and keep it to yourself.
cells.core:
In your account, you are only the one nearby while things get handled — the calls, the papers, working out what's whose. Running well, this looks like a hand that already knows the right weight of a thing and moves toward it without a committee, quietly evening what has tipped. The sense of right is exact in you, and it has not yet been claimed as yours.

Pick one small open question that's been sitting — what's owed, what's fair here — and settle it from the quiet sense inside you. Act on what it says, and keep it to yourself. No one needs to know the case is closed.
cells.sheetLine: The fair count runs through you. Keep one, unseen.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a private sense of what's owed is already operating underneath the person's account of themselves; the record only gives abundant knowing, not a count of debts. A reader could reasonably say they're not keeping any tally and simply don't know yet what to hand back. The ask survives being wrong because returning one owed object still stands on its own as a fair act. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'somebody has been keeping the quiet count' — cut.
